classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish the given side edge from face altitude, construct an altitude in each isosceles face type, and use the corresponding half-base in Pythagoras before summing face areas.

content.prompt:
Calculate the surface area of these pyramids.

The given lengths are the base lengths and the edge length. All measurements are in centimetres. Round your answers to the nearest whole square centimetre.

spec.description: Unshaded right square pyramid with all four base edges double-ticked, base edge 16 and lateral edge 20. Hidden edges are derived from explicit faces and viewing direction.
spec.mathematics: Square base side 16 cm; lateral edge 20 cm; centred apex. Face height is sqrt(20^2-8^2).

answer.worked:
The face height $l$ bisects the base edge.
$$\begin{aligned}l^2&=20^2-8^2\\l^2&=336\\l&=4\sqrt{21}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$
Area of base: $16^2=256\text{ cm}^2$.

Area of four triangles:
$$4\left(\frac12\times16\times4\sqrt{21}\right)=128\sqrt{21}\text{ cm}^2.$$
Total surface area:
$$\begin{aligned}A&=256+128\sqrt{21}\\A&\approx843\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Inverted right rectangular pyramid. Base edges 16 have single ticks; base edges 24 have double ticks. Lateral edge 32 is labelled on the right. The rear-left lateral edge is hidden.
spec.mathematics: Centred apex below a 16 cm by 24 cm rectangular base; lateral edges 32 cm. Face heights are sqrt(32^2-8^2) and sqrt(32^2-12^2).

answer.worked:
Each triangular-face height bisects its base edge.

For faces with base $16\text{ cm}$:
$$\begin{aligned}l_{16}^2&=32^2-8^2\\l_{16}^2&=960\\l_{16}&=8\sqrt{15}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$
For faces with base $24\text{ cm}$:
$$\begin{aligned}l_{24}^2&=32^2-12^2\\l_{24}^2&=880\\l_{24}&=4\sqrt{55}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$
Area of base: $16\times24=384\text{ cm}^2$.

Area of the two $16\text{ cm}$ triangles:
$$2\left(\frac12\times16\times8\sqrt{15}\right)=128\sqrt{15}\text{ cm}^2.$$
Area of the two $24\text{ cm}$ triangles:
$$2\left(\frac12\times24\times4\sqrt{55}\right)=96\sqrt{55}\text{ cm}^2.$$
Total surface area:
$$\begin{aligned}A&=384+128\sqrt{15}+96\sqrt{55}\\A&\approx1592\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Right rectangular pyramid with double-ticked front and rear base edges 40, single-ticked side base edges 25, and lateral edge 37. The view exposes three triangular faces; only the rear base edge is hidden.
spec.mathematics: Centred apex above a 40 cm by 25 cm rectangular base; lateral edges 37 cm. Face heights are sqrt(37^2-20^2) and sqrt(37^2-12.5^2).

answer.worked:
Each triangular-face height bisects its base edge.

For faces with base $40\text{ cm}$:
$$\begin{aligned}l_{40}^2&=37^2-20^2\\l_{40}^2&=969\\l_{40}&=\sqrt{969}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$
For faces with base $25\text{ cm}$:
$$\begin{aligned}l_{25}^2&=37^2-12.5^2\\l_{25}^2&=\frac{4851}{4}\\l_{25}&=\frac{\sqrt{4851}}2\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$
Area of base: $40\times25=1000\text{ cm}^2$.

Area of the two $40\text{ cm}$ triangles:
$$2\left(\frac12\times40\times\sqrt{969}\right)=40\sqrt{969}\text{ cm}^2.$$
Area of the two $25\text{ cm}$ triangles:
$$2\left(\frac12\times25\times\frac{\sqrt{4851}}2\right)=\frac{25\sqrt{4851}}2\text{ cm}^2.$$
Total surface area:
$$\begin{aligned}A&=1000+40\sqrt{969}+\frac{25\sqrt{4851}}2\\A&\approx3116\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$
